grammar.title: 百 for hundred
grammar.explanation: 百 (bǎi) means "hundred". Build numbers the same way as with 十: 一百 (100), 两百 (200) — use 两, not 二, before 百 just as with other measure words.

grammar.title: 比 for comparisons
grammar.explanation: 比 (bǐ) compares two things directly: A 比 B + adjective means "A is more [adjective] than B". Don't add 很 before the adjective in this pattern — 比 already carries the comparison.

grammar.title: 多少 for "how many/how much"
grammar.explanation: 多少 (duōshao) asks about quantity, especially larger numbers, prices, or amounts: 多少钱? ("How much money?"). Unlike 几, 多少 doesn't require a measure word before the noun, though one can still be added.

grammar.title: 二 vs 两 for the number two
grammar.pattern: 两 + measure word / 二 in counting and labels
grammar.explanation: Both 二 (èr) and 两 (liǎng) mean "two", but they aren't interchangeable. Use 两 before a measure word like 个 when counting things (两个), and use 二 for counting in sequence, dates, and labels like 二月 (February) or 第二 (second).

grammar.title: 有 for possession
grammar.explanation: 有 (yǒu) means "to have". Sentence-final 了 after 有 signals a change: the subject did not have it before but has it now.

grammar.title: 最 for superlatives
grammar.explanation: 最 (zuì) makes an adjective superlative, like English "-est" or "most". Place it directly before the adjective: 最好 (best), 最大 (biggest). No extra word for "the" is needed.

sentences.en: How many people do you have?

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu sān ge háizi.
Tā jiā yǒu wǔ ge rén.
